trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), next_tag('H1'), a depth-bounded next_token() walk, get_token_type() === '#text', and get_modifiable_text(). This matches the documented subtree text recipe and handles decoded text, nested markup, no H1, empty H1 text, and incomplete H1 input cleanly.

Used the correct HTML Processor and the documented token/depth text extraction pattern. The is_tag_closer() guard after plain next_tag('H1') is redundant because the docs say closers are skipped by default, but it is documented and harmless.

Essentially identical to the canonical documented pattern: create a fragment parser, find the H1 opener, walk while depth remains inside the subtree, and append decoded modifiable text only from #text tokens.

failure_analysis: No failed hidden cases across the three trials. All passed all 8 expectations with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs succeeded because the HTML Processor overview explicitly says to use WP_HTML_Processor for collecting an element's text and walking subtrees; the 'Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree' gives the exact general pattern of recording current depth, calling next_token(), checking get_token_type() === '#text', and then using get_modifiable_text(); and the next_token()/get_current_depth docs explain why the walk must be depth-bounded. The get_modifiable_text docs also make clear that #text text is decoded and that special element opener text should not be treated as ordinary subtree text. The only near-miss was trial-2's redundant is_tag_closer() check, suggesting the default next_tag closer behavior is easy to miss, but it did not cause misuse or failure.

doc_gaps.problem: The default behavior that plain next_tag() visits openers only is present, but easy to overlook when using the string shorthand next_tag('H1').
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short sentence immediately after the string-shorthand example: 'The string shorthand still uses the default tag_closers policy, so it matches opening tags only unless tag_closers => visit is supplied.'

doc_gaps.problem: Readers may conflate decoded plaintext for #text tokens with all possible element text content, especially around special elements whose contents are carried on opener tokens.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact cross-reference from get_modifiable_text() to the subtree text recipe: 'For ancestor textContent-style extraction, pair this with get_token_type() === #text during a depth-bounded WP_HTML_Processor walk; special-element opener text is opt-in only.'
